newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Jews give Koran to Palestinians after poster row.
newsitem.headline: Jews give Koran to Palestinians after poster row.

text.p: Jewish clergymen gave a copy of the Koran to a West Bank Palestinian school on Wednesday to try to soothe religious tensions inflamed by a poster depicting the Prophet Mohammad as a pig.

Rabbi Jeremy Milgrom, one of three Jewish religious leaders who visited al-Yaacoubia school in Hebron, said he was worried that the political conflict between Israelis and Palestinians was taking on religious connotations.

"We came to visit the school which was ransacked, to see the destruction," said Milgrom, of the Israeli Rabbis for Human Rights group. "We brought a Koran. We inscribed it and gave it to the headmistress," he said.
Palestinians were enraged over three separate incidents in which Moslem and Christian religious symbols were desecrated.

A Jewish woman faces up to 26 years in prison for putting up posters in Hebron portraying Mohammad as a pig. The posters ignited a wave of unrest in the volatile city where 400 Jews live in the heart of 100,000 Arabs.
Moslems also charged that four copies of the Koran were torn up in the Hebron school which they said was ransacked by Israeli soldiers. Israel denied soldiers were involved.
An Israeli science magazine angered Palestinian Christians by publishing a picture of the Virgin Mary with a cow's head to illustrate a story on cloning. Israel apologised.
Milgrom said he was sure that most Israelis and Jews around the world rejected the desecration of holy books of other religions.
"What is really frightening and we are very concerned that the conflict between Israelis and Palestinians will deteriorate into a religous war," Milgrom said.
The Islamic Resistance Movement Hamas charged it held the Israeli government responsible for a rise in "deliberate harming of religious feelings of Moslems and Christians".
